concepts.why: The patient presents with a painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region, which is consistent with a canal of Nuck hernia, and ultrasound findings show a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass tracking into the inguinal canal.
The patient's symptoms and ultrasound findings are also consistent with an inguinal hernia, although the presence of a canal of Nuck hernia is more specific.
The patient's mass is described as non-tender and has mild peripheral blood flow on Doppler imaging, which could be consistent with a vulvar lipoma.
The patient's mass is located in the right labia majora, which could be consistent with a bartholin gland cyst, although the size and ultrasound findings are not typical.
The patient's mass is described as a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass, which could be consistent with a vulvar fibroma.
The patient's mass is located in the right labia majora and has a well-defined border, which could be consistent with an epidermal inclusion cyst.
The patient's mass is described as a solid mass, which could be consistent with a vulvar leiomyoma.
The patient's mass has mild peripheral blood flow on Doppler imaging, which could be consistent with a vulvar hemangioma.

rationales.F01: The presence of a painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region is highly suggestive of a canal of Nuck hernia.
rationales.F08: The non-tender mass of the right labia majora extending to the right groin is consistent with a canal of Nuck hernia.
rationales.F09: The well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass measuring 90 × 44 × 55 mm in the right labia majora tracking into the inguinal canal is consistent with a canal of Nuck hernia.
rationales.F12: The preoperative impression of a canal of Nuck hernia containing omental tissue strongly supports this diagnosis.
